Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median of $1,030,000 and a remarkable 57.1% of them selling above asking price at an average of 100.6% of list price — a clear signal that inventory is essentially nonexistent and demand is overwhelming. Multi-family properties are equally sought after, with a median sale price of $1,350,000 and nearly half (47.1%) closing over ask, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant interest in a city where rental income can help offset steep acquisition costs. Even the condo market, while slightly softer with 32.6% of units selling over ask at a 99.4% SP/LP ratio, saw 46 sales in the past 30 days, making it the most active segment by volume. For sellers, this is about as favorable an environment as it gets — properly priced homes are attracting multiple offers with little to no negotiating leverage left for buyers, who should expect to come in well-prepared with strong financing, minimal contingencies, and the ability to act decisively the moment a listing hits the market.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most fiercely competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median of $2,460,000 and selling at 104.4% of list price — nearly two-thirds of them closing above asking. Condos at a $1,170,000 median and multifamilies at $2,180,000 tell a similar story of relentless demand, with virtually no available inventory to speak of across all property types. For sellers, conditions are essentially ideal — properly priced homes are generating multiple offers quickly and routinely exceeding list price, particularly in the single-family and multifamily segments. Buyers should expect to move fast, come in well above asking with strong terms, and understand that Cambridge's proximity to MIT, Harvard, and the biotech corridor means this pricing pressure is unlikely to ease anytime soon.

Milton.narrative: Milton's real estate market remains exceptionally competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,010,000 and a remarkable 109.8% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely paying nearly 10% above asking price, with 76.9% of homes selling over list. Multi-families are also moving aggressively at a $1,106,000 median with half of sales closing above asking, while condos are the relative outlier, coming in at $1,125,000 but selling at 98.2% of list price with no units going over ask. With inventory so tight that months of supply is essentially nonexistent across all categories and only 18 total sales recorded in the past 30 days, Milton is firmly a seller's market where well-priced single-families and multi-families in particular are generating intense bidding wars. Buyers should come prepared with strong offers and limited contingencies, while sellers — especially those listing single-family homes — are in an enviable position to maximize their return in one of the South Shore's most sought-after communities.

Quincy.narrative: Quincy's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $742,500 and a remarkable 68.8% of homes closing above asking price at an average of 102.2% of list price — clear signals that buyers must come prepared with strong offers and minimal contingencies. The condo market offers a relatively more accessible entry point at a $379,900 median, though even here sellers are holding firm at 100% of list price with nearly 1 in 5 units still trading over ask. Multi-family properties are commanding a $997,500 median sale price, making them an increasingly significant investment threshold, though the 98.4% SP/LP ratio suggests slightly more negotiating room compared to other segments. With no measurable months of supply across all three categories and 65 total transactions closed in the past 30 days, sellers hold a decisive advantage, while buyers should expect fast-moving timelines and be ready to act decisively in what remains one of the South Shore's tightest markets.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,110,000 and a remarkable 80% of homes selling above asking price at an average of 103.3% of list price. The condo market is notably active with 27 sales in the past 30 days and a median of $777,000, though buyers are finding slightly more breathing room there with only 22.2% of units going over ask and a sale-to-list ratio of 98.5%. Multi-families are holding firm at a median of $1,150,000 with a perfect 100% sale-to-list ratio and 40% selling above ask, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing properties. With effectively zero months of supply across all segments, sellers hold enormous leverage right now, while buyers should expect to move quickly, come in at or above list price, and have financing thoroughly buttoned up before making any offer.

Medford.narrative: Medford's real estate market is firing on all cylinders across every property type, with single families commanding a $900,000 median sale price and a striking 59.1% of homes selling above asking price, while condos and multi-families follow suit at $610,000 and $1,125,000 respectively. Sale-to-list price ratios hovering right at or above 100% across all three categories — 100.1% for single families, 100.3% for condos, and 99.6% for multi-families — confirm that virtually no negotiating room exists for buyers. With months of supply data registering as essentially zero and only 38 total transactions closed in the past 30 days, inventory is critically constrained, meaning serious buyers must come prepared with strong pre-approvals, competitive offers, and minimal contingencies. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — pricing at or slightly above market is being validated by buyers, and the multi-family segment in particular is attracting investors willing to push past the $1.1 million mark in a city that continues to benefit from its proximity to Boston and Cambridge.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose remains a fiercely competitive market across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,042,495 and selling at 105.5% of list price — nearly 77% of the 22 homes sold in the last 30 days closed above asking. Multi-family properties are even hotter, with a median of $1,099,000 and every single one of the 3 sales closing above list at an average of 110% SP/LP, signaling strong investor and house-hacker demand. Condos offer a relatively more accessible entry point at a $490,000 median, though even that segment is selling right at list price with 20% of units going over ask. For buyers, the absence of any measurable months of supply means you should expect multiple-offer situations and need to come in aggressively with clean terms, while sellers across all property types are in an exceptionally strong position to maximize their return with minimal negotiating pressure.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's single-family market is operating at a fever pitch, with a median sale price of $1,365,000 and a staggering 73.9% of homes closing above asking price at an average of 105.1% of list price — a clear signal that buyers are entering virtually every offer situation expecting a bidding war. The condo segment offers a slightly more measured pace, with a median of $787,500 and 38.9% of units selling over ask, though the 99.5% sale-to-list ratio still reflects strong demand with very little room to negotiate. Multi-families are commanding a median of $1,380,000, and while only three sold in the past 30 days, a third of those still closed above asking despite a more modest 96.5% SP/LP ratio, suggesting investor appetite remains active but selective. With essentially no measurable months of supply across all property types, sellers hold an overwhelming advantage right now, while buyers should be prepared to move fast, waive contingencies strategically, and bring their strongest offers to the table from the start.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,867,000 and selling exactly at list price on average — though half of all homes are actually trading above ask, a clear sign that well-priced properties are generating competitive offers. The condo market may be the hottest segment in town, with 80% of units closing over asking price and a median sale-to-list ratio of 104.8%, while condos are moving at a median of $760,000. Multi-family properties are equally competitive, with 75% selling above list and a median of $1,232,500, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand across all property types. With essentially no months of supply across every category and only 23 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight — sellers who price strategically can expect swift, multi-offer scenarios, while buyers should come prepared to waive contingencies, move quickly, and anticipate paying above list price in virtually every segment.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is operating at a fever pitch, with a median sale price of $2,087,500 and 53.8% of homes selling above asking price at an average of 100.6% of list — all against essentially zero months of supply, signaling an acutely inventory-starved environment. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $620,000 median, though even that segment sees a third of units closing over ask, underscoring broad demand across all price points in this highly desirable suburb. For buyers, Winchester demands aggressive preparation — pre-approval, waived contingencies, and swift decision-making are near-essential to compete — while sellers across all property types are in an exceptionally strong position to command top dollar with minimal concessions. The multi-family segment, with just one sale at $1,367,500, has too thin a sample to draw firm conclusions, but the lack of inventory there mirrors the broader market dynamic that continues to define Winchester as one of Greater Boston's most competitive towns.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $895,492 and selling exactly at list price on average — and nearly half of all single-family sales, 48.9%, closing above asking price in the last 30 days. The condo market is equally active, with 340 units sold in the past month at a median of $768,500 and a 98.8% sale-to-list ratio, while multi-family properties are leading the pack at a $1.2 million median with 37.5% of sales going over ask. With months of supply data effectively at zero across all categories, inventory is critically tight, pointing to a market where demand is dramatically outpacing available homes. For buyers, this means coming in prepared with strong financing, competitive offers above list price, and minimal contingencies; for sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — well-priced properties are moving quickly and often sparking bidding wars regardless of asset class.
